root_cause.text: In the act8945a charger driver, `devm_request_irq()` was called before `devm_power_supply_register()`, so the IRQ handler could run while `charger->psy` was still uninitialized during probe or already freed during devm cleanup, causing `power_supply_changed()` to use an invalid `power_supply` pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `devm_request_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, act8945a_status_changed, ...)` from before to after `charger->psy = devm_power_supply_register(...)`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that reverse-order devm teardown lets an interrupt fire after the `power_supply` handle has been freed but before IRQ unregistration, and also before the handle is registered during probe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop registering the charger status IRQ handler during probe so initialization no longer depends on requesting that interrupt.
intent_record.what: The probe function removes a devm_request_irq() call that registered act8945a_status_changed as a falling-edge interrupt handler for the charger IRQ, along with the associated error check, log message, and early return on failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the charger driver no longer requests or installs that IRQ handler during probe, so probe will not fail due to IRQ request errors and the driver will stop receiving interrupt-driven status change notifications through this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the ACT8945A charger IRQ during probe and fail initialization if interrupt setup cannot be completed.
intent_record.what: A new devm_request_irq() call was added in act8945a_charger_probe() to register the given IRQ with act8945a_status_changed as the handler, using IRQF_TRIGGER_FALLING and the name "act8945a_interrupt"; on failure, the code now logs an error and returns the error code before continuing.
intent_record.how: At probe time, the charger driver now requests and installs its interrupt handler so falling-edge nIRQ events can be delivered to act8945a_status_changed at runtime; if IRQ setup fails, probe aborts instead of leaving the device initialized without interrupt handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change removes registration of the charger status IRQ during probe, directly preventing the IRQ handler from running while `charger->psy` is uninitialized or during teardown, which addresses the reported ordering/lifetime bug.

The change directly concerns when and how the ACT8945A charger IRQ is requested during probe. Since the root cause is incorrect ordering of devm_request_irq() relative to devm_power_supply_register(), any change to IRQ registration in probe is directly tied to the vulnerable initialization sequence.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct cause: the IRQ handler is registered before the power supply object is registered, allowing the interrupt handler to run while charger->psy is still uninitialized or later during teardown after it has been freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement registers the IRQ handler before the power supply is registered, creating a race where act8945a_status_changed() can call power_supply_changed() using charger->psy while it is still uninitialized during probe or already freed during devm teardown.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full probe/remove ordering, the IRQ handler, and the deferred work that uses the power_supply pointer. The vulnerable construct is present: in act8945a_charger_probe(), IRQ is requested before the power supply is registered: `ret = devm_request_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, act8945a_status_changed, ... , charger);` appears before `charger->psy = devm_power_supply_register(&pdev->dev, &act8945a_charger_desc, &psy_cfg);`. The IRQ path ultimately dereferences `charger->psy`: `act8945a_status_changed()` does `schedule_work(&charger->work);` and `act8945a_work()` calls `power_supply_changed(charger->psy);`. Although the handler checks `if (charger->init_done)`, that only blocks execution until probe finishes; it does not solve the devm cleanup ordering problem described in the root cause. On device teardown, `devm_power_supply_register()` resources are released before the earlier `devm_request_irq()` resource, because devm cleanup is unwound in reverse registration order. That means the IRQ can still fire after the power supply has been freed but before the IRQ is released, and the handler can schedule work that calls `power_supply_changed(charger->psy)` on an invalid pointer. The added `.remove` method sets `charger->init_done = false; cancel_work_sync(&charger->work);`, but it does not free the IRQ before the devm power_supply cleanup, so the core ordering bug remains. Therefore the function contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the full fix.
